output.brief:
The October night premium shortfalls were caused by a pay rule change, not by your data. On 22 Oct an Ardentra consultant applied a template to rule NSP-02. It moved the night premium start from 20:00 to 22:00. The change was logged as a "label correction, no calculation impact" and wasn't tested. The platform's audit trail can't be edited, and it shows this was the only calculation rule edit. Internal audit recalculated pay for all 158 night workers. 147 were underpaid, and each shortfall equals the premium for 20:00–22:00 to within a penny. The 11 workers paid correctly are on 22:00–06:00 shifts. Re-running October in the test tenant with the start time set back to 20:00 gave correct pay for all 158. Flagged records were not underpaid more often than unflagged ones.

What to do: don't suspend the HR team, and don't do the full reload or accept the clause 14.3 cost. Have Ardentra restore the 20:00 start and prove it in a test re-run before 24 Nov. Then make off-cycle payments to everyone underpaid. Ask Ardentra to cover the cost. Don't roll back release 7.4. The overtime drop is probably linked to the pay problem, but the rota trial may also contribute. Reassess that after pay is corrected.
